title: The False Drawer
verdict: Marcus Vale was responsible for the disappearance of a reel of microfilm.
intent: Marcus Vale wanted to hide an old correction notice before a lawsuit review.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the night editor approved the discard cart after the reel was last scanned.
Remove a reel of microfilm from its checked location.
Hide the item in a cardboard tube marked as discarded posters.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a reel of microfilm disappeared from a newspaper archive basement during digitization.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the emergency light blinked twice before the flicker.
The physical trace was silver film dust on the discard cart.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a film splicer with new tape.
The item could be concealed in a cardboard tube marked as discarded posters.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the night editor knew the emergency circuit timing.
distractor_cues: a retired reporter searching old stories
a technician opening the breaker panel
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
